subject: ENGLISH
title: Whose Is It? · M01 D16
objective: Use possessive pronouns to show ownership.
introduction: Whose kite is that? Mine! Whose bag is this? Yours! Use mine, yours, his, hers, ours, and theirs to show who owns things.

vocabulary.definition: Showing who owns something, like Milo's.
A word that names a person, place, or thing, like kite or bag.
A group of words that tells a complete idea, like “The kite is hers.”

items.prompt: Which sentence shows ownership the right way?
items.explanation: Mine stands alone: “The red bag is mine.” We do not say “mine bag,” and “is her” is missing the s — hers is the right word.

items.prompt: Which one uses “ours” the right way?
items.explanation: Ours stands alone at the end: “That desk is ours.” We do not put ours before desk, and “is our” is missing the s.
“This is mine bag” is wrong because mine stands alone — say “my bag” or “this bag is mine.” The other sentences are correct.
Hers stands alone: “The kite is hers.” “The kite is her” is missing the s, and “the hers kite” puts hers before the noun.
Theirs stands alone at the end: “The blue hats are theirs.” We do not say “theirs blue hats” or “them hats.”
